newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FAA says Thailand meets air safety standards.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FAA says Thailand meets air safety standards.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration on Monday rated Thailand's civil aviation authority in compliance with international air safety standards, lifting the rating from conditional.
The FAA surveyed Thailand's civil aviation authority last August and gave it a conditional rating because it did not meet all International Civil Aviation Organization safety standards.
The FAA said that, after improvements and a new survey last December, Thailand was given the compliance rating.

It said the ratings were not assessments of whether or not a nation's airlines were safe, but whether foreign civil aviation authorities were in place to maintain operational safety standards by foreign carriers.
A conditional rating means that operations by foreign airlines to the United States are permitted only under heightened FAA inspection, the FAA said.
The United States is reviewing the civil aviation authorities of all countries with flights into the United States or who ask for such assessments.
